name: Selvage Strip Leggings (Scrap-Knit)
description: Hand-knit or loomed from strips of salvaged fabric selvage and jersey offcuts, these leggings are thick, uneven, and colorful in a chaotic way — stripes and textures that follow whatever material was available. Worn under shorts, skirts, or oversized tops. Common in the Gray Zone among people who have a little skill and access to scrap bins. Surprisingly durable.
what_it_says: You made this, or someone you trust made this. There's skill in poverty that the upper tiers don't see.
worn_by: young women in the Gray Zone
manufacturer: Self-made / the Gray Zone craft market
story_hooks: A particular pattern of selvage strips is recognizable as coming from a specific closed factory — someone's tracking where the materials went.
The crafter who makes these has started encoding short messages in the stripe sequences — it's become a coded communication network.

physical_description.visual_profile: Chunky, hand-crafted legwear with an intentionally chaotic aesthetic—irregular vertical stripes and woven texture that reads as both utilitarian and artisanal. Sits close to the leg with slight gathering at ankles. Gives an impression of resourcefulness and creative resilience.
physical_description.fit: Fitted through hip and thigh, tapered at ankle with gentle bunching. Compression-adjacent without being restrictive—follows body contours while accommodating layering underneath.
physical_description.primary_material: Recycled jersey knit blended with salvaged textile selvage strips; hand-loomed or machine-assisted construction using scrap-bin materials
physical_description.texture: Thick, uneven ribbed weave with visible knit irregularities; slightly nubby surface from mixed fiber composition; some areas softer (jersey) and others stiffer (selvage edges)
physical_description.color_scheme: Chaotic multicolor stripe pattern—burnt orange, faded teal, charcoal, muddy yellow, industrial gray layered randomly. No two pairs identical. Matte finish with occasional sheen variation from fiber type differences
physical_description.closures: Elastic waistband (salvaged, often a contrasting color); friction-fit at ankle with intentional loose edge or minimal cuff
distinctive_features: Hand-visible knit inconsistencies and dropped stitches left as design feature
Visible selvage edge details woven into stripes
No branding or labels—purely functional markers of maker
Likely reinforced at high-wear areas (inner thigh, calf) with patch layering
Ankle cuff often unfinished or raw-edged for authentic scrap aesthetic
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 / the Gray Zone craft—signals sub-grade maker economy, creative poverty, skilled hands
physical_description.cultural_context: Street-tier self-sufficiency; worn by the Gray Zone dwellers, waste-stream salvagers, and anti-corpo craftspeople. Communicates rejection of mass-manufacture and investment in DIY skill. Associated with off-grid communities in the GLMZ ungoverned zones.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn-in from first wear—pilling expected, minor snags normalized, slight stretching at waistband over time. Patched repairs visible and accepted as part of garment evolution
